title: Rectangular protrusion
spec: Create a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to zero and a translation vector also set to zero. On this coordinate system, draw a new face and create a closed loop with four lines. The first line starts at the origin and ends at coordinates [0.75, 0.0]. The second line extends vertically from [0.75, 0.0] to [0.75, 0.0214]. The third line moves horizontally from [0.75, 0.0214] to [0.0, 0.0214], and the fourth line completes the rectangle by connecting [0.0, 0.0214] back to the origin. After drawing the closed loop, apply a scaling factor of 0.75 to the entire sketch. Ensure that the scaled sketch remains aligned with the original coordinate system by setting the rotation angles to zero and the translation vector to zero. To transform the 2D sketch into a 3D model, extrude the sketch along the normal direction with a depth of 0.0214 units. Set the opposite extrusion depth to zero to create a solid body. The resulting rectangular protrusion has a length of 0.75 units, a width of 0.0214 units, and a height of 0.0214 units.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create a sketch with the specified lines
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.75, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.75, 0.0214) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0214) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch to create the final shape
r = r.extrude(0.0214)

# The final model is represented as 'r'
